_note: A dependant with severe disability — "₹ 125000" for "₹ 75000" (s.127(3), p.163): s.127(1): a resident individual "shall be allowed a deduction up to ₹ 75000 … if during that year he has (a) incurred expenditure for the medical treatment (including nursing), training and rehabilitation of a dependant, being a person with disability; or (b) paid or deposited any amount under a scheme … for the maintenance of a dependant" (pp.162–163); "dependant" — the spouse, children, parents, brothers and sisters "dependant wholly or mainly" on the individual (s.127(9)(b)); not one who claimed s.154 (s.127(8)); the certificate with the return (s.127(6)–(7)) and (2)'s scheme conditions are entry conditions. ChapterEightNode allows the lesser of the amount spent or deposited and this limit — "up to" read as a ceiling (OQ-19); more than one disabled dependant is refused (OQ-19). rulebook DED-80DD-001. Old regime only (s.202(2)(a)(xii), p.227). TY 2026-27 and TY 2025-26; the 1961 counterpart, s.80DD, is the TY 2025-26 version (W-075d3). D-138. The "lesser of" is in the cap since W-075d3 (LeastOf), not the node (D-146). TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.80DD(1) proviso (thc p.343): for a dependant with severe disability, "one hundred and twenty-five thousand rupees" for "seventy-five thousand rupees" — a fixed sum (Fixed 125000), as the row above. sources/2026-10-07-chapter-via.md B14. D-146. In every regime as a row; the new regime forbids it through DIS-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION, whose basis REG-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION (S2 s.202(2)(a); 1961 s.115BAC(2)(i)) every explanation cites (D-166).
